article_notes: 140 EDTA samples from practitioners and a diagnostic laboratory (Masovia, Poland); groups healthy (39), B. canis (82), D. repens (12), co-infected (7). Severity was graded from laboratory values (Bajer et al. 2016). Gene expression (Figs 1-3) was measured in a random subset of 32 B. canis dogs split into 'Babesia 1' (mild/moderate) and 'Babesia 2' (severe); no per-group numbers and the Babesia 1 vs 2 pairwise tests are not reported, so those rows are low confidence. Note the text describes Babesia 1 as 'classes 0 and 1' but earlier as mild and moderate levels; this is inconsistent. Table 3 gives per-level means for B. canis-only dogs; extracted as descriptive (level 2 vs level 0). Co-infection with D. repens is compared with B. canis single infection for marker values (Tables 1 and 3), but the distribution of co-infected dogs across severity levels is not reported, so co-infection was not extracted as a severity factor. Sample timing relative to treatment not stated.

severity_definitions.label: 'Babesia 2' (severe babesiosis) vs 'Babesia 1' (mild/moderate babesiosis)
severity_definitions.definition: Severity classification based on Bajer et al. (2016): anaemia (RBC), hepatic (AST/ALT/ALP) and renal (urea) scores 0-2; any score 2 = severe (level 3, n=44 of 82); more than one dysfunction at level 1 = moderate (n=16); one group of signs = mild (n=22). For gene expression, a random subset of 32 B. canis dogs was split into Babesia 1 (mild and moderate) and Babesia 2 (severe); subset group sizes not stated.
severity_definitions.quote: B. canis-infected dogs with mild and moderate babesiosis (representing classes 0 and 1) were combined into the group referred to as ‘Babesia 1’ and dogs with severe babesiosis (class 2) were assigned to ‘Babesia 2’.

severity_definitions.label: anaemia level 2 (RBC <4.5 T/l) vs level 0 (RBC 5.5-8.0 T/l)
severity_definitions.definition: Anaemia severity score from RBC count: 0 = 5.5-8.0 T/l, 1 = 4.5-5.5 T/l, 2 = below 4.5 T/l. Rows use the B. canis-only column of Table 3 (level 2 vs level 0).
severity_definitions.severe_group: B. canis dogs at anaemia level 2 (n not stated)
severity_definitions.comparison_group: B. canis dogs at anaemia level 0 (n not stated)
severity_definitions.quote: a. severity of anaemia (severity score 0—RBC counts within normal range 5.5–8.0 T/l; severity score 1—RBC counts in a range 4.5–5.5 T/l; severity score 2—RBC below 4.5 T/l)

severity_definitions.label: hepatic dysfunction level 2 vs level 0
severity_definitions.definition: Hepatic score from AST, ALT and ALP: within reference range = 0, above (up to 100 U/l) = 1, profoundly above (>100 U/l) = 2. Rows use the B. canis-only column of Table 3.
severity_definitions.severe_group: B. canis dogs at hepatic level 2 (n not stated)
severity_definitions.comparison_group: B. canis dogs at hepatic level 0 (n not stated)
severity_definitions.quote: b. hepatic dysfunction parameters (measures of enzymes activity) based on reference values for AST– aspartate aminotransferase, ALT- alanine aminotransferase and ALP- alkaline phosphatase within, above (up to 100 U/l) and profoundly above (> 100 U/l) the normal range, representing scores of 0, 1 and 2, respectively (Table 2)

severity_definitions.label: renal dysfunction level 2 vs level 0
severity_definitions.definition: Renal score from serum urea: within reference = 0, above (up to 100 mg/dl) = 1, profoundly above (>100 mg/dl) = 2. Rows use the B. canis-only column of Table 3.
severity_definitions.severe_group: B. canis dogs at renal level 2 (n not stated)
severity_definitions.comparison_group: B. canis dogs at renal level 0 (n not stated)
severity_definitions.quote: c. renal dysfunction parameters (based on reference values for serum urea) within, above (up to 100 mg/dl) and profoundly above (> 100 mg/dl) the normal range, representing severity scores of 0, 1 and 2, respectively (Table 2).

associations.quote: The highest INF-γ expression was found in the group of dogs with severe babesiosis (Babesia 2) in contrast to the low expression level in dogs with mild/moderate babesiosis (Babesia 1).
associations.note: Relative mRNA expression (2^-ddCt, normalised to 3 healthy dogs) shown only in a figure; no per-group numbers. Kruskal-Wallis across all groups (healthy, Babesia 1, Babesia 2, D. repens, co-infected). Significance reported only between D. repens and Babesia 2; Babesia 1 vs Babesia 2 test not reported.

associations.quote: and differences in expression between groups were not statistically significant (Fig. 1B)
associations.note: Relative mRNA expression (2^-ddCt, normalised to 3 healthy dogs) shown only in a figure; no per-group numbers. Kruskal-Wallis across all groups (healthy, Babesia 1, Babesia 2, D. repens, co-infected). Lowest expression in Babesia 2 per text.

associations.quote: The highest level of expression was found in dogs with mild/moderate babesiosis (Babesia 1) and the lowest in dogs with advanced babesiosis (Babesia 2).
associations.note: Relative mRNA expression (2^-ddCt, normalised to 3 healthy dogs) shown only in a figure; no per-group numbers. Kruskal-Wallis across all groups (healthy, Babesia 1, Babesia 2, D. repens, co-infected). No test result stated for Babesia 1 vs Babesia 2.

associations.quote: However, the differences in expression between groups were not statistically significant (Fig. 2B).
associations.note: Relative mRNA expression (2^-ddCt, normalised to 3 healthy dogs) shown only in a figure; no per-group numbers. Kruskal-Wallis across all groups (healthy, Babesia 1, Babesia 2, D. repens, co-infected). Lowest expression in Babesia 1 per text.

associations.quote: Although the differences in IL-13 gene expression between groups were not statistically significant
associations.note: Relative mRNA expression (2^-ddCt, normalised to 3 healthy dogs) shown only in a figure; no per-group numbers. Kruskal-Wallis across all groups (healthy, Babesia 1, Babesia 2, D. repens, co-infected).

associations.quote: The highest level of SOCS3 expression was detected in dogs with severe babesiosis (Babesia 2)
associations.note: Relative mRNA expression (2^-ddCt, normalised to 3 healthy dogs) shown only in a figure; no per-group numbers. Kruskal-Wallis across all groups (healthy, Babesia 1, Babesia 2, D. repens, co-infected). Significant difference among all groups; Discussion says SOCS3 was 'expressed significantly higher' in Babesia 2, but the pairwise Babesia 1 vs Babesia 2 result is not reported.

associations.quote: Relatively high and similar expression of IL-10 was found in dogs with mild/moderate and severe babesiosis (Fig. 3). Differences in the level of IL-10 gene expression between groups were not statistically significant (Fig. 3).
associations.note: Relative mRNA expression (2^-ddCt, normalised to 3 healthy dogs) shown only in a figure; no per-group numbers. Kruskal-Wallis across all groups (healthy, Babesia 1, Babesia 2, D. repens, co-infected). Text is inconsistent: the summary paragraph says IL-10 expression was highest in Babesia 1.
